claims.text: The proposed catalyst is a platinum-nickel alloy with an FCC crystal structure.
Combining electrochemical characterization with DFT simulations can optimize the platinum-nickel catalyst design.
The intervention produces an optimized catalyst surface structure.
The intervention produces optimized electronic properties.
Optimized surface structure and electronic properties enhance hydrogen adsorption.
Optimized surface structure and electronic properties enhance hydrogen desorption.
Enhanced hydrogen adsorption and desorption improve HER and HOR catalytic activity.
Enhanced hydrogen adsorption and desorption improve catalyst durability.
The platinum-nickel catalyst will have a 20% higher exchange current density than pure platinum.
The platinum-nickel catalyst will have a 30% lower Tafel slope than pure platinum.
Performance is to be evaluated at 25°C, 1 atm, and in 0.5 M sulfuric acid.
Performance may vary with experimental conditions and the accuracy of the DFT simulations.

contradictions.description: The predicted exchange-current improvement is 20% (1.2 times pure platinum), but the falsification rule uses a threshold of less than 1.5 times pure platinum. This threshold does not directly test the stated 20% prediction and, because it is combined with the Tafel criterion using 'and,' many failures of the predicted outcome would not falsify the hypothesis.
